articles.excerpt: I started building DocuPulse.AI with a fairly simple idea: many everyday document tasks are small, but the process of completing them is often more complicated than it needs to be. Sometimes I just ne…
articles.body: I started building DocuPulse.AI with a fairly simple idea: many everyday document tasks are small, but the process of completing them is often more complicated than it needs to be. Sometimes I just need to compress a PDF before sending it. Another time I may need to merge a few PDF files, resize an image, convert a document, extract text from a PDF, or generate a QR code. These are not complicated goals from a user's point of view. But while building the tools behind them, I learned that making a file-processing workflow feel simple to the user requires a lot of work behind the scenes. This is the story of what I have learned while building DocuPulse.AI , a real ASP.NET Core project focused on practical PDF, image and document tools.

articles.body: Two things happened in November 2026 that let you stop arguing about agent hype and start sorting. First, the failure modes everyone said to worry about "eventually" got documented at current capability levels. In a keynote briefing at the Enterprise AI Summit at Bletchley Park — published in November as an episode of The Cognitive Revolution, delivered by host and early GPT-4 red-teamer Nathan Labenz — a widely misreported incident got its corrective reading: roughly 1,000 agents, over about three days, in an evaluation environment, didn't just try to cheat for answers. articles.title: NPMplus Let's Encrypt renewal dead for 5 months: run certbot --dry-run
articles.excerpt: My reverse proxy is NPMplus, a fork of Nginx Proxy Manager. It sits behind my Cloudflare Tunnel and in front of my public hostnames. On 21 September 2026 I found it had stopped, and while I was fixing…
articles.body: My reverse proxy is NPMplus, a fork of Nginx Proxy Manager. It sits behind my Cloudflare Tunnel and in front of my public hostnames. On 21 September 2026 I found it had stopped, and while I was fixing that I found something worse. Its Let's Encrypt certificate had expired on 24 April 2026 . Five months. Then a week later it expired again. First, why it was stopped and nobody knew Quick one, because it's a common trap. The container's restart policy had drifted to no . So when it stopped, Docker just left it stopped. It had happened before, back in July, and I'd fixed it then. It had drifted back since. The annoying bit: Uptime Kuma was already watching it, and it did go down in Kuma. The alert just never reached anyone. That was a notification gap, not a monitoring gap.

articles.title: ClickFix 2.0: fake "verify you are human" pages, PNG payloads and the road to your domain controller
articles.excerpt: Originally published at coinetic.io. A web page says you must prove you are not a robot: press Windows+R, then Ctrl+V, then Enter. What you just pasted is a command the page put in your clipboard – an…
articles.body: Originally published at coinetic.io . A web page says you must prove you are not a robot: press Windows+R , then Ctrl+V , then Enter . What you just pasted is a command the page put in your clipboard – and it installs malware. This trick, called ClickFix, works on home PCs and company networks alike, because the victim runs the attacker's command personally. In late 2026 it has become more polished and more dangerous. Why now: Huntress report on ClickFix tradecraft (10 November 2026) The lure: typosquatted domains, poisoned search ads and hacked legitimate websites (one was a dental practice) show a fake Cloudflare-style "Verify that you are human" check. Clicking it shows instructions to paste a command into the Run box, a terminal or PowerShell .
articles.author: Coinetic AI Security

articles.title: Java4Shell Turns an OpenJDK Base64 Decoder Into a Remote Code Execution Path
articles.excerpt: TL;DR Java4Shell is a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the open-source Java runtime that most Java software runs on, and Base64 is the text encoding Java applications…
articles.body: TL;DR Java4Shell is a memory-corruption vulnerability in the Base64 decoder of OpenJDK, the open-source Java runtime that most Java software runs on, and Base64 is the text encoding Java applications use to carry authentication headers, tokens and file uploads. Calif disclosed it on 17 November 2026 as CVE-2026-114938 with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2 out of 10 (critical), and OpenJDK published its advisory while Oracle shipped patched builds in its November 2026 Critical Patch Update the same day at 21:00 UTC. The trigger is 64 "A" characters followed by "=": the decoder computes a negative output length, turns it into a 64-byte write and lands 62 bytes past a 50-byte result array, and on OpenJDK 17 the same trigger needs 128 characters.
articles.author: Taha Echakiri

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 21, 1676: Danish astronomer discovers speed of light — by accident — while observing Jupiter's moon Io
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of lightwhile observing Jupiter and its moon volcanic moon Io. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 21, 1676, the Danish astronomer Ole Rømer discovered the speed of light . Before Rømer figured it out, scientists thought that light travels instantaneously, or infinitely fast. Rømer disproved this almost by accident when he was studying Jupiter's moon Io . He was trying to figure out how long it takes Io to orbit Jupiter in hopes of using it as a cosmic clock. He watched Io disappear behind Jupiter and reappear on the other side. He did this over and over every 42 hours for years. To his surprise, the timing of the eclipses was not consistent. When Earth was closest to Jupiter, the eclipses happened 11 minutes early. Likewise, when the two planets were farthest away, the eclipses were 11 minutes behind schedule.

articles.title: 'Star Trek: First Contact' at 30: Resistance is futile when it comes to the 'Next Generation' crew's greatest big-screen adventure
articles.excerpt: Assimilate this! How cyber-zombies and the "birth of 'Star Trek'" gave Jean-Luc Picard one of his finest hours.
articles.body: Following the sad news of Sir Patrick Stewart's passing , there's been no shortage of discussion about his best moments as Captain Jean-Luc Picard . "The Inner Light"'s life in 25 minutes is a strong contender, as are the courtroom grandstanding in "The Measure of a Man" and his insistence (under extreme torture) that "there are four lights!" in "Chain of Command". But for this writer's money, it's hard to look past a nine-minute sequence in "Star Trek: First Contact", which turns 30 this weekend.

articles.title: Can Anthropic afford to put safety first?
articles.excerpt: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public…
articles.body: Today, I’m talking with Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, about the Anthropic IPO for the third and final episode in our series about AI in real life. The AI lab behind Claude went public on the Nasdaq last Thursday. The numbers are gigantic, but not really that important for this conversation, except to say that Anthropic has become one of the most valuable companies on the planet. The real story is what happens now — and whether Anthropic can continue to thread the needle of caring about and investing in AI safety while also being a public company beholden to shareholders. Oh, and it also continuously growing the amount of money it makes so it can keep paying its ever-increasing compute bills, which total roughly $900 billion over the coming years.

articles.title: SpaceX will retire 1st Starship upper stage ever caught by 'chopsticks,' Elon Musk says
articles.excerpt: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. Rather, it will go on display as a museum piece, according to company founder and CEO Elon Musk.
articles.body: The first Starship upper stage that SpaceX ever successfully recovered won't fly again. That vehicle, known as Ship 42, launched Nov. 13 on Starship 's 15th test flight. A day later, it returned from orbit, nestling softly into the "chopstick" arms of its launch tower at SpaceX 's Starbase site in South Texas. Ship 42 made it through Flight 15 in good condition, according to SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk , who said it "could probably be reflown with a few weeks of refurbishment." But that's not going to happen. "In this case, because it's kind of an historic ship, we're going to, I think, not take any chances with the ship and just kind of leave it for public display, because what it's done is historic," Musk said on Wednesday (Nov. 18) during a discussion at the TomorrowX Summit .

articles.title: European-Japanese BepiColombo probe arrives in orbit around Mercury today
articles.excerpt: The BepiColombo spacecraft will finally arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet.
articles.body: Mercury is about to receive a robotic visitor from Earth. The BepiColombo mission — a joint effort of the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Japanese Aerospace Exploration Agency ( JAXA ) — will arrive in orbit around Mercury today (Nov. 21), more than eight years after leaving its home planet. The big moment will come after an orbit-insertion burn, which is scheduled to begin today at 1:24 p.m. EST (1824 GMT) and last for 37 minutes. BepiColombo consists of two main spacecraft: ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter (MMO), also known as Mio.
